newsitem.title: UK: REUTERS PROFITS HIT BY POUND, SETS BUYBACK.
newsitem.headline: REUTERS PROFITS HIT BY POUND, SETS BUYBACK.

text.p: Reuters Holdings Plc on Wednesday reported a three percent fall in first half pre-tax profit due to the strong pound and said it would buy back shares worth up to 200 million pounds ($335.8 million).

Pre-tax profit in the six months ended June 30 was 333 million pounds, down from 342 million a year earlier, but profits rose by 12 percent excluding exchange rate effects. Chief executive Peter Job said underlying revenue growth was in line with 1996 and was expected to carry on at around this level for 1997 as a whole.

Revenue fell by 29 million pounds to 1.41 billion but rose by eight percent if comparable exchange rates were used. Reuters said underlying margins were maintained despite the cost of rolling out the new 3000 product range.
The company said it did not expect the strong pound to impact its marketing positioning adversely, but currency factors were likely to continue to restrict reported revenue and earnings.
Job said the recent UK budget resulted in a more level playing field for shareholders in relation to share buybacks, although advance corporation tax (ACT) remained a major constraint.

He said the company would carry out a share repurchase programme "to return up to 200 million, which is possible within our ACT constraints. We continue to review developments in this area in relation to a more substantial return of cash." Net funds grew by 71 million pounds to 1.12 billion in the six months.

Reuters said information products grew revenue by seven percent year on year at comparable exchange rates and improved market share. Installations of the 3000 series, slow to begin with, picked up strongly.
Transaction products revenue grew by 10 percent at comparable rates, with revenue at Instinet, the electronic equity brokerage, ahead by 17 percent.
Revenue from the Dealing 2000 foreign exchange products rose by four percent at comparable rates.

"The strategy of focusing on the needs of financial markets continues to be rewarding, and the pace of new product enhancements is helping us to fill gaps and find new market segments. Underlying revenue growth is in line with that of 1996 and we expect it to carry on at around this level for 1997 as a whole," Job said.
The interim dividend was raised by 13 percent to 3.1 pence.
